intro: This is where Anatolia learned to write. You are at Kültepe, ancient Kanesh, a mound in Kayseri province whose story reaches back to the 3rd millennium BC. Here an Assyrian trading colony left behind Anatolia's first written documents.
history: Assyrian merchants came here and founded a karum, a trading colony. They left behind over 23,000 cuneiform tablets, found on this very site, and with them begins the written history of Anatolia.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Karum quarter and the Palace remains, then the Tablet archives and the Mound itself.
facts: Did you know? Among the tablets is one of the world's earliest known marriage contracts. Anatolia met writing here: the 23,000-plus cuneiform tablets left by Assyrian merchants are the earliest written documents from Anatolia. Yet they are not epic but bookkeeping — promissory notes, partnership contracts, court records, letters home. One merchant's wife writes telling him to send better cloth. And the karum at the foot of the mound was a separate merchants' quarter, one of the earliest known international trading colonies.
outro: This brings our tour of Kültepe, ancient Kanesh, to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
